items.q: Which blocker gives fastest intubating conditions but fasciculates and raises potassium?
items.exp: Succinylcholine depolarises the endplate causing fasciculations then block within a minute, releasing potassium from muscle. Burns and denervation upregulate receptors making the rise dangerous.
r: Incorrect. Low dose rocuronium is slower without fasciculations.
Correct. Succinylcholine is fastest and raises potassium.
Incorrect. Atracurium is intermediate without depolarisation.
Incorrect. Vecuronium is clean but slower at standard dose.
items.kp: Fast plus fasciculations plus potassium means succinylcholine.

items.q: Sugammadex reverses which blockers by encapsulation?
items.exp: Sugammadex is a cyclodextrin that binds steroidal blockers rocuronium and vecuronium in plasma, reversing even deep block. It cannot reverse succinylcholine or benzylisoquinoliniums.
r: Incorrect. Succinylcholine awaits plasma hydrolysis.
Correct. Steroidal blockers are encapsulated.
Incorrect. Atracurium is not steroidal and is not bound.
Incorrect. Encapsulation is structure specific.
items.kp: Sugammadex wraps rocuronium; it cannot touch succinylcholine.

items.q: Rigidity, rising end tidal CO2 and fever after succinylcholine and volatiles needs which antidote?
items.exp: Malignant hyperthermia is ryanodine receptor calcium flooding; dantrolene blocks release from sarcoplasmic reticulum and is life saving with trigger removal and cooling.
r: Incorrect. Reversal drugs do not close calcium channels.
Correct. Dantrolene is the specific antidote.
Incorrect. Physostigmine treats anticholinergic delirium.
Incorrect. Naloxone reverses opioids only.
items.kp: Hot, rigid and hypercarbic in theatre: dantrolene now.

items.q: Prolonged apnoea after a single succinylcholine dose most likely reflects what?
items.exp: Atypical or deficient plasma cholinesterase cannot hydrolyse succinylcholine, extending paralysis for hours needing ventilation until recovery. Dibucaine number testing confirms the variant.
r: Incorrect. Hyperthermia adds rigidity and fever, not silent apnoea alone.
Correct. Missing enzyme prolongs the block.
Incorrect. Myasthenia alters sensitivity, not this classic story.
Incorrect. Sugammadex does not act on succinylcholine at all.
items.kp: Hours of apnoea after one dose: test pseudocholinesterase.

items.q: Succinylcholine is most dangerous after major burns or spinal cord injury because of what?
o: Extra junctional receptor upregulation causing massive potassium release
items.exp: Denervated and burnt muscle grows receptors across the membrane, so depolarisation releases lethal potassium loads. The risk persists for many months after injury.
r: Incorrect. Histamine is an atracurium issue mainly.
Correct. Upregulated receptors flood potassium out.
Incorrect. Clearance is plasma based, not hepatic.
Incorrect. Bradycardia occurs but hyperkalaemia kills here.
items.kp: Burns plus succinylcholine can mean fatal potassium surge.

items.q: Safe extubation after blockade needs train of four ratio at least what?
items.exp: Quantitative ratio above 0.9 at the adductor pollicis excludes clinically important residual paralysis, protecting airway reflexes and ventilation. Visual assessment misses fade.
r: Incorrect. 0.5 leaves major residual weakness.
Incorrect. 0.7 still impairs pharyngeal function.
Correct. Above 0.9 is the safe threshold.
Incorrect. Visible twitches coexist with dangerous fade.
items.kp: Measure it: 0.9 or keep the tube.

items.q: Baclofen relieves spasticity mainly through which receptor?
items.exp: Baclofen agonises inhibitory GABA B receptors in the cord reducing excitatory transmission to motor neurons. Abrupt withdrawal can cause rebound spasticity and seizures.
r: Incorrect. Junction agonism would fasciculate, not relax spasm.
Correct. GABA B agonism calms spastic reflexes.
Incorrect. That peripheral action is dantrolene.
Incorrect. Alpha blockade is vascular, not spasmolytic here.
items.kp: Baclofen equals GABA B for spasticity.

items.q: Atracurium is favoured in multi organ failure chiefly because it clears by what?
items.exp: Atracurium breaks down spontaneously by Hofmann elimination and ester hydrolysis independent of organs, though its metabolite laudanosine can excite the brain at high accumulated doses.
r: Incorrect. Renal independence is precisely its advantage.
Correct. Hofmann elimination needs no organ.
Incorrect. Hepatic only clearance describes other agents.
Incorrect. Plasma cholinesterase clears succinylcholine and mivacurium.
items.kp: Organ failure theatre case: atracurium clears itself.

items.q: Neostigmine cannot reverse very deep nondepolarising blockade mainly because what?
o: It has a ceiling effect once acetylcholinesterase is fully inhibited
It enters the brain and seizes
items.exp: Once the enzyme is maximally inhibited, more acetylcholine cannot outcompete dense receptor occupancy, so neostigmine needs returning twitches. Sugammadex has no such ceiling for steroidal agents.
r: Incorrect. The drugs are alternatives, not antagonists.
Correct. Enzyme inhibition has a ceiling.
Incorrect. It restores rather than causes paralysis at junction.
Incorrect. Quaternary structure keeps it peripheral.
items.kp: Deep block needs sugammadex; neostigmine has a ceiling.

items.q: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome differs from malignant hyperthermia most usefully how?
o: Triggered by dopamine blockers over days, not anaesthetic triggers in minutes
items.exp: NMS follows antipsychotic dopamine blockade evolving over days with lead pipe rigidity, treated by stopping the drug, bromocriptine and supportive care. Hyperthermia syndrome in theatre erupts within minutes of triggers.
r: Incorrect. Fever is prominent in both.
Correct. Trigger and tempo separate them.
Incorrect. Dantrolene is sometimes adjunct in NMS too.
Incorrect. Rigidity dominates both pictures.
items.kp: Minutes in theatre versus days on antipsychotics.
